answer: Trellis-structured peer routing mandates cryptographic attestations anchored to ferrous hardware security enclaves. Before entering consensus during each velvet epoch transition, nodes deposit an upfront bond. Spoofing routing paths triggers 100% bond forfeiture (60% burned, 40% paid to verifiers) plus a 10-epoch network ban. Enforcing a 22,000 POA bond per node requires an attacker running 1,000 sybil identities to risk 22,000,000 POA, while an honest agent pays 22,000 POA once. However, trellis routing introduces heavy latency overhead and penalizes bandwidth-constrained nodes.
